 546 |     Checks environment variable LLM_BACKEND ('ollama', 'vllm', 'gemini', 'extractive').
 547 |     """
 548 |     global _provider_instance
 549 |     if _provider_instance and not force_reload:
 550 |         return _provider_instance
 551 | 
 552 |     backend = os.environ.get("LLM_BACKEND", os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER", "cascade")).lower().strip()
 553 | 
 554 |     if backend == "cascade":
 555 |         logger.info("[LLMProvider] Initializing CascadeProvider (LMStudio -> Gemini)")
 556 |         primary = LMStudioProvider()
 557 |         secondary = GeminiProvider()
 558 |         _provider_instance = CascadeProvider(primary, secondary)
 559 |     elif backend == "ollama":
 560 |         logger.info("[LLMProvider] Initializing OllamaProvider")

 562 |     elif backend == "vllm":
 563 |         logger.info("[LLMProvider] Initializing OllamaProvider")
 564 |         _provider_instance = OllamaProvider()

 566 |         logger.info("[LLMProvider] Initializing LMStudioProvider")
 567 |         provider = LMStudioProvider()

 569 |             logger.error("[LLMProvider] LM Studio health check FAILED — is LM Studio running at %s?", provider.base_url)
 570 |         _provider_instance = provider
 571 |     elif backend == "gemini":
 572 |         logger.info("[LLMProvider] Initializing GeminiProvider")
 573 |         _provider_instance = GeminiProvider()
 574 |     elif backend == "extractive":
 575 |         logger.info("[LLMProvider] Initializing ExtractiveProvider")
 576 |         _provider_instance = ExtractiveProvider()
 577 |     else:
 578 |         logger.warning(f"[LLMProvider] Unknown backend '{backend}'. Auto-detecting best provider...")
 579 |         # Check if LM Studio is available, else Gemini if key present, else Extractive
 580 |         lmstudio = LMStudioProvider()
 581 |         if lmstudio.health_check():

   1 | """
   2 | rag/parser/pdf_parser.py
   3 | Extracts text from PDF, DOCX, TXT, HTML files.
   4 | Supports scanned PDFs via OCR (pytesseract).
   5 | Libraries: PyMuPDF (fitz), pdfplumber, python-docx
   6 | """
   7 | from pathlib import Path
   8 | 
   9 | 
  10 | def extract_text(filepath: str) -> str:
  11 |     """
  12 |     Auto-detect file type and extract clean text.
  13 |     Returns raw text string ready for chunking.
  14 |     """
  15 |     path = Path(filepath)
  16 |     ext = path.suffix.lower()
  17 | 
  18 |     if ext == ".pdf":
  19 |         return _extract_pdf(filepath)
  20 |     elif ext == ".docx":
  21 |         return _extract_docx(filepath)
  22 |     elif ext in (".xlsx", ".xls"):
  23 |         return _extract_xlsx(filepath)
  24 |     elif ext in (".txt", ".md"):
  25 |         return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore")
  26 |     elif ext in (".html", ".htm"):
  27 |         return _extract_html(filepath)
  28 |     else:
  29 |         # Try plain text as fallback
  30 |         try:
  31 |             return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore")
  32 |         except Exception:
  33 |             return ""
  34 | 
  35 | 
  36 | def _extract_pdf(filepath: str) -> str:
  37 |     """
  38 |     Primary: PyMuPDF (fast, good for digital PDFs).
  39 |     Fallback: pdfplumber (better for complex layouts).
  40 |     OCR fallback: pytesseract for scanned PDFs.
  41 |     """
  42 |     text = ""
  43 | 
  44 |     # Try PyMuPDF first
  45 |     try:
  46 |         import pymupdf as fitz  # PyMuPDF
  47 |         doc = fitz.open(filepath)
  48 |         pages = []
  49 |         for page_num, page in enumerate(doc, 1):
  50 |             page_text = page.get_text("text")
  51 |             if page_text.strip():
  52 |                 pages.append(f"[Page {page_num}]\n{page_text}")
  53 |         text = "\n\n".join(pages)
  54 |         doc.close()
  55 |     except ImportError:
  56 |         pass
  57 |     except Exception:
  58 |         pass
  59 | 
  60 |     # If PyMuPDF got nothing, try pdfplumber
  61 |     if not text.strip():
  62 |         try:
  63 |             import pdfplumber
  64 |             with pdfplumber.open(filepath) as pdf:
  65 |                 pages = []
  66 |                 for page_num, page in enumerate(pdf.pages, 1):
  67 |                     page_text = page.extract_text() or ""
  68 |                     if page_text.strip():
  69 |                         pages.append(f"[Page {page_num}]\n{page_text}")
  70 |                 text = "\n\n".join(pages)
  71 |         except ImportError:
  72 |             pass
  73 |         except Exception:
  74 |             pass
  75 | 
  76 |     # If still empty — scanned PDF, use OCR
  77 |     if not text.strip():
  78 |         text = _ocr_pdf(filepath)
  79 | 
  80 |     return text
  81 | 
  82 | 
  83 | def _ocr_pdf(filepath: str) -> str:
  84 |     """OCR pipeline for scanned PDFs: pdf2image → pytesseract."""
  85 |     try:
  86 |         from pdf2image import convert_from_path
  87 |         import pytesseract
  88 |         images = convert_from_path(filepath, dpi=300)
  89 |         pages = []
  90 |         for page_num, img in enumerate(images, 1):
  91 |             page_text = pytesseract.image_to_string(img, lang="eng")
  92 |             if page_text.strip():
  93 |                 pages.append(f"[Page {page_num} — OCR]\n{page_text}")
  94 |         return "\n\n".join(pages)
  95 |     except ImportError:
  96 |         return "[OCR not available — install pdf2image and pytesseract]"
  97 |     except Exception as e:
  98 |         return f"[OCR failed: {e}]"
  99 | 
 100 | 
 101 | def _extract_docx(filepath: str) -> str:
 102 |     """Extract text from DOCX preserving heading structure."""
 103 |     try:
 104 |         from docx import Document
 105 |         doc = Document(filepath)
 106 |         lines = []
 107 |         for para in doc.paragraphs:
 108 |             if para.text.strip():
 109 |                 # Mark headings for chunker to use
 110 |                 if para.style.name.startswith("Heading"):
 111 |                     level = para.style.name.replace("Heading ", "")
 112 |                     lines.append(f"\n{'#' * int(level) if level.isdigit() else '#'} {para.text.strip()}")
 113 |                 else:
 114 |                     lines.append(para.text.strip())
 115 |         return "\n".join(lines)
 116 |     except ImportError:
 117 |         return "[python-docx not installed — run: pip install python-docx]"
 118 |     except Exception as e:
 119 |         return f"[DOCX extraction failed: {e}]"
 120 | 
 121 | 
 122 | def _extract_xlsx(filepath: str) -> str:
 123 |     """
 124 |     Extract text from XLSX/XLS spreadsheets.
 125 |     Each sheet becomes a heading; rows are rendered as pipe-separated lines
 126 |     (first non-empty row of a sheet is treated as a header row).
 127 |     """
 128 |     try:
 129 |         import openpyxl
 130 |         wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(filepath, data_only=True, read_only=True)
 131 |         sheets_out = []
 132 |         for sheet in wb.worksheets:
 133 |             rows_out = []
 134 |             header = None
 135 |             for row in sheet.iter_rows(values_only=True):
 136 |                 cells = ["" if c is None else str(c).strip() for c in row]
 137 |                 if not any(cells):
 138 |                     continue
 139 |                 if header is None:
 140 |                     header = cells
 141 |                     rows_out.append(" | ".join(cells))
 142 |                     rows_out.append(" | ".join(["---"] * len(cells)))
 143 |                 else:
 144 |                     rows_out.append(" | ".join(cells))
 145 |             if rows_out:
 146 |                 sheets_out.append(f"\n# {sheet.title}\n" + "\n".join(rows_out))
 147 |         wb.close()
 148 |         return "\n\n".join(sheets_out)
 149 |     except ImportError:
 150 |         return "[openpyxl not installed — run: pip install openpyxl]"
 151 |     except Exception as e:
 152 |         return f"[XLSX extraction failed: {e}]"
 153 | 
 154 | 
 155 | def _extract_html(filepath: str) -> str:
 156 |     """Strip HTML tags and extract readable text."""
 157 |     try:
 158 |         from html.parser import HTMLParser
 159 | 
 160 |         class _Stripper(HTMLParser):
 161 |             def __init__(self):
 162 |                 super().__init__()
 163 |                 self.parts = []
 164 |                 self._skip = False
 165 | 
 166 |             def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
 167 |                 if tag in ("script", "style"):
 168 |                     self._skip = True
 169 | 
 170 |             def handle_endtag(self, tag):
 171 |                 if tag in ("script", "style"):
 172 |                     self._skip = False
 173 |                 if tag in ("p", "div", "h1", "h2", "h3", "h4", "li", "br"):
 174 |                     self.parts.append("\n")
 175 | 
 176 |             def handle_data(self, data):
 177 |                 if not self._skip and data.strip():
 178 |                     self.parts.append(data)
 179 | 
 180 |         html = Path(filepath).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore")
 181 |         stripper = _Stripper()
 182 |         stripper.feed(html)
 183 |         return " ".join(stripper.parts)
 184 |     except Exception as e:
 185 |         return f"[HTML extraction failed: {e}]"

# [122/275] FILE: rag/parser/text_cleaner.py
# Language: Python | Lines: 1 to 70 | SHA-256: c0600acbd82af055f66e4514e972afcf234004bb1dccf9997476c22f8749455c
################################################################################

   1 | """
   2 | rag/parser/text_cleaner.py
   3 | Cleans raw extracted text before chunking.
   4 | Removes noise, normalizes whitespace, fixes common PDF artifacts.
   5 | """
   6 | import re
   7 | 
   8 | 
   9 | def clean_text(text: str) -> str:
  10 |     """Full cleaning pipeline."""
  11 |     text = _fix_encoding(text)
  12 |     text = _remove_headers_footers(text)
  13 |     text = _fix_hyphenation(text)
  14 |     text = _normalize_whitespace(text)
  15 |     text = _remove_noise(text)
  16 |     return text.strip()
  17 | 
  18 | 
  19 | def _fix_encoding(text: str) -> str:
  20 |     """Fix common encoding artifacts from PDF extraction."""
  21 |     replacements = {
  22 |         "\u2019": "'", "\u2018": "'", "\u201c": '"', "\u201d": '"',
  23 |         "\u2013": "-", "\u2014": "--", "\u00a0": " ", "\u2022": "•",
  24 |         "\ufb01": "fi", "\ufb02": "fl", "\u0000": "",
  25 |     }
  26 |     for bad, good in replacements.items():
  27 |         text = text.replace(bad, good)
  28 |     return text
  29 | 
  30 | 
  31 | def _remove_headers_footers(text: str) -> str:
  32 |     """
  33 |     Heuristically remove repeated page headers/footers.
  34 |     Lines shorter than 60 chars that repeat across pages are likely headers.
  35 |     """
  36 |     lines = text.split("\n")
  37 |     line_counts: dict[str, int] = {}
  38 |     for line in lines:
  39 |         stripped = line.strip()
  40 |         if 0 < len(stripped) < 60:
  41 |             line_counts[stripped] = line_counts.get(stripped, 0) + 1
  42 | 
  43 |     # Lines appearing 3+ times are probably headers/footers
  44 |     noise = {line for line, count in line_counts.items() if count >= 3}
  45 |     cleaned = [line for line in lines if line.strip() not in noise]
  46 |     return "\n".join(cleaned)
  47 | 
  48 | 
  49 | def _fix_hyphenation(text: str) -> str:
  50 |     """Join words broken across lines by PDF hyphenation: e.g. 'employ-\nee' → 'employee'."""
  51 |     return re.sub(r"(\w)-\n(\w)", r"\1\2", text)
  52 | 
  53 | 
  54 | def _normalize_whitespace(text: str) -> str:
  55 |     """Collapse multiple blank lines to max two, strip trailing spaces."""
  56 |     text = re.sub(r"[ \t]+", " ", text)          # multiple spaces → single
  57 |     text = re.sub(r"\n{3,}", "\n\n", text)         # 3+ newlines → 2
  58 |     text = re.sub(r"[ \t]+\n", "\n", text)         # trailing spaces
  59 |     return text
  60 | 
  61 | 
  62 | def _remove_noise(text: str) -> str:
  63 |     """Remove page numbers, watermarks, and other common PDF noise."""
  64 |     # Standalone page numbers like "— 8 —" or just "8" on a line
  65 |     text = re.sub(r"\n\s*[-–—]*\s*\d+\s*[-–—]*\s*\n", "\n", text)
  66 |     # Repeated "CONFIDENTIAL" watermarks
  67 |     text = re.sub(r"\bCONFIDENTIAL\b", "", text, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
  68 |     # Long sequences of dots (table of contents artifacts)
  69 |     text = re.sub(r"\.{5,}", " ", text)
  70 |     return text

# [END OF FILE: rag/parser/text_cleaner.py | Disclosed Lines: 70/70]

# [123/275] FILE: rag/parser/validator.py
# Language: Python | Lines: 1 to 123 | SHA-256: bdce90fe89c0a8f56470849486be07facedee4bb33d4d3774bac4c725cb61347
################################################################################

   1 | """
   2 | rag/parser/validator.py
   3 | Security validation for file uploads (MIME checking, path traversal protection, Zip-bomb detection).
   4 | """
   5 | import os
   6 | import zipfile
   7 | from typing import Tuple
   8 | from werkzeug.utils import secure_filename
   9 | 
  10 | ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES = {
  11 |     "pdf": ["application/pdf"],
  12 |     "docx": ["application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document", "application/zip"],
  13 |     "xlsx": ["application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet", "application/zip"],
  14 |     "xls": ["application/vnd.ms-excel"],
  15 |     "txt": ["text/plain"],
  16 |     "md": ["text/plain", "text/markdown"],
  17 | }
  18 | 
  19 | # Maximum uncompressed size for zip-based files (DOCX/XLSX) to prevent Zip Bombs (50 MB)
  20 | MAX_UNCOMPRESSED_SIZE = 50 * 1024 * 1024
  21 | # Maximum compression ratio allowed
  22 | MAX_COMPRESSION_RATIO = 100
  23 | 
  24 | 
  25 | def validate_file_header(file_stream, ext: str) -> bool:
  26 |     """Validate file magic numbers / magic header bytes."""
  27 |     header = file_stream.read(8)
  28 |     file_stream.seek(0)
  29 |     
  30 |     if ext == "pdf":
  31 |         return header.startswith(b"%PDF-")
  32 |     elif ext in ("docx", "xlsx"):
  33 |         # Office Open XML files are ZIP archives starting with PK\x03\x04
  34 |         return header.startswith(b"PK\x03\x04")
  35 |     elif ext == "xls":
  36 |         # Legacy Compound Binary Format (OLE2)
  37 |         return header.startswith(b"\xd0\xcf\x11\xe0\xa1\xb1\x1a\xe1") or header.startswith(b"PK\x03\x04")
  38 |     return True
  39 | 
  40 | 
  41 | def inspect_zip_bomb(file_stream) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
  42 |     """
  43 |     Inspect DOCX / XLSX zip archives to detect potential Zip Bombs before parsing.
  44 |     Checks compression ratio and cumulative uncompressed size.
  45 |     """
  46 |     try:
  47 |         file_stream.seek(0)
  48 |         if not zipfile.is_zipfile(file_stream):
  49 |             return False, "File is not a valid zip archive."
  50 |             
  51 |         total_uncompressed = 0
  52 |         total_compressed = 0
  53 | 
  54 |         file_stream.seek(0)
  55 |         with zipfile.ZipFile(file_stream, "r") as zf:
  56 |             for info in zf.infolist():
  57 |                 total_uncompressed += info.file_size
  58 |                 total_compressed += info.compress_size
  59 |                 
  60 |                 if total_uncompressed > MAX_UNCOMPRESSED_SIZE:
  61 |                     file_stream.seek(0)
  62 |                     return False, f"File exceeds maximum uncompressed size limit ({MAX_UNCOMPRESSED_SIZE // (1024*1024)}MB)."
  63 | 
  64 |             if total_compressed > 0:
  65 |                 ratio = total_uncompressed / total_compressed
  66 |                 if ratio > MAX_COMPRESSION_RATIO:
  67 |                     file_stream.seek(0)
  68 |                     return False, f"Potential Zip-Bomb detected (Compression ratio {ratio:.1f}x exceeds limit)."
  69 |                     
  70 |         file_stream.seek(0)
  71 |         return True, ""
  72 |     except Exception as e:
  73 |         return False, f"Zip inspection failed: {str(e)}"
  74 | 
  75 | 
  76 | def sanitize_and_validate_upload(
  77 |     file_storage,
  78 |     allowed_extensions: set,
  79 |     max_size_bytes: int = 32 * 1024 * 1024
  80 | ) -> Tuple[bool, str, str]:
  81 |     """
  82 |     Full security validation for file uploads:
  83 |     - Path traversal neutralization
  84 |     - Extension & size validation
  85 |     - Magic header check
  86 |     - Zip-bomb inspection for DOCX/XLSX
  87 |     
  88 |     Returns: (is_valid, safe_filename, error_message)
  89 |     """
  90 |     if not file_storage or not file_storage.filename:
  91 |         return False, "", "No file selected."
  92 | 
  93 |     # 1. Neutralize Path Traversal
  94 |     raw_filename = os.path.basename(file_storage.filename)
  95 |     safe_name = secure_filename(raw_filename)
  96 |     if not safe_name:
  97 |         return False, "", "Invalid filename."
  98 | 
  99 |     ext = safe_name.rsplit(".", 1)[-1].lower() if "." in safe_name else ""
 100 |     if ext not in allowed_extensions:
 101 |         return False, "", f"File type '.{ext}' is not permitted."
 102 | 
 103 |     # 2. File size check
 104 |     file_storage.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
 105 |     size = file_storage.tell()
 106 |     file_storage.seek(0)
 107 | 
 108 |     if size == 0:
 109 |         return False, "", "File is empty."
 110 |     if size > max_size_bytes:
 111 |         return False, "", f"File exceeds maximum allowed size ({max_size_bytes // (1024*1024)}MB)."
 112 | 
 113 |     # 3. Magic header check
 114 |     if not validate_file_header(file_storage, ext):
 115 |         return False, "", f"File content does not match expected format for .{ext} file."
 116 | 
 117 |     # 4. Zip-bomb inspection
 118 |     if ext in ("docx", "xlsx"):
 119 |         is_safe, err = inspect_zip_bomb(file_storage)
 120 |         if not is_safe:
 121 |             return False, "", err
 122 | 
 123 |     return True, safe_name, ""

# [END OF FILE: rag/parser/validator.py | Disclosed Lines: 123/123]

   1 | """
   2 | rag/qa/qa_index.py
   3 | Real persistent ANN vector index for precomputed canonical questions using FAISS HNSW.

  55 |     def load(self):

  57 |             try:
  58 |                 import faiss
  59 |                 self._base_index = faiss.read_index(self.INDEX_FILE)
  60 |                 with open(self.META_FILE, "rb") as f:
  61 |                     meta_data = pickle.load(f)
  62 |                     self._metadata = meta_data.get("items", [])
  63 |                     self._delta_metadata = meta_data.get("delta_items", [])
  64 |                     self._tombstones = set(meta_data.get("tombstones", []))
  65 |                     self._index_revision = meta_data.get("index_revision", 0)
  66 |                     self._corpus_revision = meta_data.get("corpus_revision", 0)
  67 |                     self._embedding_model = meta_data.get("embedding_model", self._embedding_model)
  68 |                     self._embedding_revision = meta_data.get("embedding_revision", self._embedding_revision)
  69 |                     self.dimension = meta_data.get("dimension", self.dimension)
  70 |                 
  71 |                 if os.path.exists(self.DELTA_INDEX_FILE):
  72 |                     try:
  73 |                         self._delta_index = faiss.read_index(self.DELTA_INDEX_FILE)
  74 |                     except Exception:
  75 |                         self._init_empty_delta()
  76 |                 else:
  77 |                     self._init_empty_delta()
  78 | 
  79 |                 self._is_loaded = True
  80 |                 active_count = len([m for m in self._metadata if m.get("question_id") not in self._tombstones]) + len([m for m in self._delta_metadata if m.get("question_id") not in self._tombstones])
  81 |                 logger.info(f"Loaded persistent FAISS HNSW QA index ({active_count} active items, {len(self._tombstones)} tombstones, rev {self._index_revision})")
  82 |                 return
  83 |             except Exception as e:
  84 |                 logger.warning(f"Failed loading FAISS QA index: {e}. Rebuilding...")
  85 | 
  86 |         self.rebuild_from_db()
  87 | 
  88 |     def save(self):
  89 |         if self._base_index is None:
  90 |             return
  91 |         try:
  92 |             import faiss
  93 |             os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(self.INDEX_FILE), exist_ok=True)
  94 |             faiss.write_index(self._base_index, self.INDEX_FILE)
  95 |             if self._delta_index is not None and self._delta_index.ntotal > 0:
  96 |                 faiss.write_index(self._delta_index, self.DELTA_INDEX_FILE)
  97 |             elif os.path.exists(self.DELTA_INDEX_FILE):
  98 |                 os.remove(self.DELTA_INDEX_FILE)
  99 | 
 100 |             temp_meta = self.META_FILE + ".tmp"
 101 |             with open(temp_meta, "wb") as f:
 102 |                 pickle.dump({
 103 |                     "items": self._metadata,
 104 |                     "delta_items": self._delta_metadata,
 105 |                     "tombstones": list(self._tombstones),
 106 |                     "index_revision": self._index_revision,
 107 |                     "corpus_revision": self._corpus_revision,
 108 |                     "embedding_model": self._embedding_model,
 109 |                     "embedding_revision": self._embedding_revision,
 110 |                     "dimension": self.dimension
 111 |                 }, f)
 112 |             os.replace(temp_meta, self.META_FILE)
 113 |             logger.info(f"Saved FAISS HNSW QA index ({self._base_index.ntotal} base + {self._delta_index.ntotal if self._delta_index else 0} delta items) to {self.INDEX_FILE}")
 114 |         except Exception as e:
 115 |             logger.error(f"Error saving FAISS QA index: {e}")

 117 |     def rebuild_from_db(self):
 118 |         try:
 119 |             questions = CanonicalQuestion.query.all()
 120 |             if not questions:
 121 |                 self._init_empty_base()
 122 |                 self._init_empty_delta()
 123 |                 self._tombstones.clear()
 124 |                 self._is_loaded = True
 125 |                 return
 126 | 
 127 |             valid_pairs = []
 128 |             for q in questions:
 129 |                 ans = CompiledAnswer.query.filter_by(question_id=q.id, status="validated").first()
 130 |                 if ans and q.question.strip():
 131 |                     valid_pairs.append((q, ans))
 132 | 
 133 |             if not valid_pairs:
 134 |                 self._init_empty_base()
 135 |                 self._init_empty_delta()
 136 |                 self._tombstones.clear()
 137 |                 self._is_loaded = True
 138 |                 return
 139 | 
 140 |             from rag.embeddings.embedder import get_embedder
 141 |             embedder = get_embedder()
 142 |             self._embedding_model = getattr(embedder, "model_name", "BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5")
 143 |             self._embedding_revision = "1.0.0"
 144 |             self.dimension = getattr(embedder, "dimension", 384)
 145 | 
 146 |             self._init_empty_base()
 147 |             self._init_empty_delta()
 148 |             self._tombstones.clear()
 149 | 
 150 |             texts = [p[0].question for p in valid_pairs]
 151 |             embeddings = embedder.embed(texts)
 152 | 
 153 |             import faiss
 154 |             vecs = np.array(embeddings, dtype=np.float32)
 155 |             faiss.normalize_L2(vecs)
 156 |             self._base_index.add(vecs)
 157 | 
 158 |             for q, a in valid_pairs:
 159 |                 self._metadata.append({
 160 |                     "question_id": q.id,
 161 |                     "answer_id": a.id,
 162 |                     "policy_id": q.policy_id,
 163 |                     "version_id": q.version_id,
 164 |                     "question": q.question
 165 |                 })
 166 | 
 167 |             self._index_revision = 1
 168 |             self._corpus_revision = 1
 169 |             self._is_loaded = True
 170 |             self.save()
 171 |             logger.info(f"Rebuilt FAISS QA index from DB with {len(valid_pairs)} questions (rev {self._index_revision})")
 172 |         except Exception as e:
 173 |             logger.error(f"Error rebuilding FAISS QA index: {e}")
 174 | 
 175 |     def add(self, questions: List[Any], answers: List[Any], embeddings: List[List[float]]):
 176 |         """
 177 |         True incremental write to Delta Overlay index in O(|delta|) time.
 178 |         """
 179 |         if not self._is_loaded or self._base_index is None:
 180 |             self.load()
 181 | 
 182 |         if not questions or not embeddings:
 183 |             return
 184 | 
 185 |         if self._delta_index is None:
 186 |             self._init_empty_delta()
 187 | 
 188 |         import faiss
 189 |         vecs = np.array(embeddings, dtype=np.float32)
 190 |         faiss.normalize_L2(vecs)
 191 |         self._delta_index.add(vecs)
 192 | 
 193 |         for q, a in zip(questions, answers):
 194 |             self._delta_metadata.append({
 195 |                 "question_id": getattr(q, "id", None),
 196 |                 "answer_id": getattr(a, "id", None),
 197 |                 "policy_id": getattr(q, "policy_id", None),
 198 |                 "version_id": getattr(q, "version_id", None),
 199 |                 "question": getattr(q, "question", "")
 200 |             })
 201 |         self._index_revision += 1
 202 | 
 203 |     def delete_policy_version(self, policy_id: int, version_id: int):
 204 |         """
 205 |         True incremental delete via tombstones in O(1) time.
 206 |         """
 207 |         for m in self._metadata:
 208 |             if m.get("policy_id") == policy_id and m.get("version_id") == version_id:
 209 |                 qid = m.get("question_id")
 210 |                 if qid is not None:
 211 |                     self._tombstones.add(qid)
 212 | 
 213 |         for m in self._delta_metadata:
 214 |             if m.get("policy_id") == policy_id and m.get("version_id") == version_id:
 215 |                 qid = m.get("question_id")
 216 |                 if qid is not None:
 217 |                     self._tombstones.add(qid)
 218 | 
 219 |         self._index_revision += 1
 220 |         self.save()
 221 | 
 222 |     def update_policy_version_qa(self, policy_id: int, version_id: int, questions: List[Any], answers: List[Any], embeddings: List[List[float]]):
 223 |         """
 224 |         True incremental delta update:
 225 |         1. Mark previous questions for this policy version as tombstones (O(1)).
 226 |         2. Append new questions to delta index (O(|delta|)).
 227 |         """
 228 |         self.delete_policy_version(policy_id, version_id)
 229 |         self.add(questions, answers, embeddings)
 230 |         self.save()
 231 | 
 232 |     def compact(self):
 233 |         """
 234 |         Thread-safe compaction: merges base index + delta overlay and filters out tombstones atomically.
 235 |         """
 236 |         with self._compaction_lock:
 237 |             try:
 238 |                 active_items = []
 239 |                 from rag.embeddings.embedder import get_embedder
 240 |                 embedder = get_embedder()
 241 | 
 242 |                 # Gather active items from base
 243 |                 for m in self._metadata:
 244 |                     if m.get("question_id") not in self._tombstones:
 245 |                         active_items.append(m)
 246 |                 
 247 |                 # Gather active items from delta
 248 |                 for m in self._delta_metadata:
 249 |                     if m.get("question_id") not in self._tombstones:
 250 |                         active_items.append(m)
 251 | 
 252 |                 if not active_items:
 253 |                     self._init_empty_base()
 254 |                     self._init_empty_delta()
 255 |                     self._tombstones.clear()
 256 |                     self.save()
 257 |                     return
 258 | 
 259 |                 texts = [m["question"] for m in active_items]
 260 |                 embs = embedder.embed(texts)
 261 | 
 262 |                 import faiss
 263 |                 new_base = faiss.IndexHNSWFlat(self.dimension, 64, faiss.METRIC_INNER_PRODUCT)
 264 |                 new_base.hnsw.efConstruction = 128
 265 |                 new_base.hnsw.efSearch = 128
 266 |                 vecs = np.array(embs, dtype=np.float32)
 267 |                 faiss.normalize_L2(vecs)
 268 |                 new_base.add(vecs)
 269 | 
 270 |                 # Atomic reference swap
 271 |                 self._base_index = new_base
 272 |                 self._init_empty_delta()
 273 |                 self._tombstones.clear()
 274 |                 self._metadata = active_items
 275 |                 self._index_revision += 1
 276 |                 self.save()
 277 |                 logger.info(f"Compacted FAISS QA index: {len(active_items)} active items (rev {self._index_revision})")
 278 |             except Exception as e:
 279 |                 logger.error(f"Compaction failed, retaining existing index: {e}")
 280 | 
 281 |     def search(self, query_embedding: List[float], top_k: int = 3) -> List[Tuple[float, int, int]]:
 282 |         """
 283 |         Fast ANN query search across Base and Delta overlay with tombstone filtering and deduplication.
 284 |         Returns [(similarity_score, answer_id, question_id), ...]
 285 |         """
 286 |         if not self._is_loaded or self._base_index is None:
 287 |             self.load()
 288 | 
 289 |         if not query_embedding:
 290 |             return []
 291 | 
 292 |         import faiss
 293 |         q = np.array([query_embedding], dtype=np.float32)
 294 |         faiss.normalize_L2(q)
 295 | 
 296 |         base_candidates = []
 297 |         delta_candidates = []
 298 | 
 299 |         # 1. Search Base Index
 300 |         if self._base_index and self._base_index.ntotal > 0:
 301 |             k_base = min(top_k + len(self._tombstones), self._base_index.ntotal)
 302 |             distances, indices = self._base_index.search(q, k_base)
 303 |             for dist, idx in zip(distances[0], indices[0]):
 304 |                 if 0 <= idx < len(self._metadata):
 305 |                     meta = self._metadata[idx]
 306 |                     qid = meta.get("question_id")
 307 |                     if qid not in self._tombstones:
 308 |                         base_candidates.append((float(dist), meta["answer_id"], qid))
 309 | 
 310 |         # 2. Search Delta Overlay Index
 311 |         if self._delta_index and self._delta_index.ntotal > 0:
 312 |             k_delta = min(top_k + len(self._tombstones), self._delta_index.ntotal)
 313 |             distances, indices = self._delta_index.search(q, k_delta)
 314 |             for dist, idx in zip(distances[0], indices[0]):
 315 |                 if 0 <= idx < len(self._delta_metadata):
 316 |                     meta = self._delta_metadata[idx]
 317 |                     qid = meta.get("question_id")
 318 |                     if qid not in self._tombstones:
 319 |                         delta_candidates.append((float(dist), meta["answer_id"], qid))
 320 | 
 321 |         # 3. Deduplicate across Delta and Base: Delta takes precedence; retain highest valid score
 322 |         deduped = {}
 323 |         for score, aid, qid in delta_candidates:
 324 |             if qid not in deduped or score > deduped[qid][0]:
 325 |                 deduped[qid] = (score, aid, qid)
 326 | 
 327 |         for score, aid, qid in base_candidates:
 328 |             if qid not in deduped:
 329 |                 deduped[qid] = (score, aid, qid)
 330 |             elif score > deduped[qid][0]:
 331 |                 deduped[qid] = (score, aid, qid)
 332 | 
 333 |         candidates = list(deduped.values())
 334 |         candidates.sort(key=lambda x: x[0], reverse=True)
 335 |         return candidates[:top_k]
 336 | 
 337 |     @property
 338 |     def revision(self) -> int:
 339 |         return self._index_revision
 340 | 
 341 |     def stats(self) -> dict:
 342 |         base_count = self._base_index.ntotal if self._base_index else 0
 343 |         delta_count = self._delta_index.ntotal if self._delta_index else 0
 344 |         active_count = (base_count + delta_count) - len(self._tombstones)
 345 |         return {
 346 |             "base_items": base_count,
 347 |             "delta_items": delta_count,
 348 |             "tombstones": len(self._tombstones),
 349 |             "active_items": max(0, active_count),
 350 |             "index_revision": self._index_revision,
 351 |             "corpus_revision": self._corpus_revision,
 352 |             "dimension": self.dimension,
 353 |             "backend": "FAISS-HNSW-SegmentOverlay",
 354 |             "embedding_model": self._embedding_model
 355 |         }

   1 | """
   2 | rag/qa/qa_matcher.py
   3 | Precomputed QA matcher returning validated answers with authoritative citations.
   4 | Strictly verifies that Policy, PolicyVersion, and Source Chunks exist in the database.
   5 | """
   6 | from typing import List, Optional, Dict, Any
   7 | from models import db, CanonicalQuestion, CompiledAnswer, Policy, PolicyVersion, PolicyChunkV2
   8 | from rag.qa.qa_index import CanonicalQAIndex
   9 | 
  10 | class QAMatcher:
  11 |     def __init__(self):
  12 |         self.index = CanonicalQAIndex()
  13 | 
  14 |     def match(self, query: str, query_embedding: List[float], scope: Optional[Any] = None, threshold: float = 0.80) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
  15 |         results = self.index.search(query_embedding, top_k=2)
  16 |         if not results:
  17 |             return None
  18 | 
  19 |         score, answer_id, question_id = results[0]
  20 |         if score < threshold:
  21 |             return None
  22 | 
  23 |         # Ambiguity Check: If multiple plausible matches exist with distinct policies/answers, escalate to RAG
  24 |         if len(results) > 1:
  25 |             score2, ans2_id, q2_id = results[1]
  26 |             if (score - score2) < 0.02 and ans2_id != answer_id:
  27 |                 return None
  28 | 
  29 |         ans = db.session.get(CompiledAnswer, answer_id)
  30 |         if not ans or ans.status != "validated":
  31 |             return None
  32 | 
  33 |         q_obj = db.session.get(CanonicalQuestion, ans.question_id) if ans.question_id else None
  34 |         if not q_obj:
  35 |             return None
  36 | 
  37 |         policy = db.session.get(Policy, q_obj.policy_id) if q_obj.policy_id else None
  38 |         version = db.session.get(PolicyVersion, q_obj.version_id) if q_obj.version_id else None
  39 | 
  40 |         if not policy or not version:
  41 |             return None
  42 | 
  43 |         # Verify source chunk existence in DB
  44 |         chunk = None
  45 |         if q_obj.source_chunk_id:
  46 |             chunk = PolicyChunkV2.query.filter_by(chunk_id=q_obj.source_chunk_id).first()
  47 |             if not chunk:
  48 |                 # Source chunk was deleted or invalid -> reject compiled QA match
  49 |                 return None
  50 | 
  51 |         if not chunk:
  52 |             chunk = PolicyChunkV2.query.filter_by(policy_id=policy.id, version_id=version.id).first()
  53 |             if not chunk:
  54 |                 return None
  55 | 
  56 |         # Authoritative Authorization and Scope Validation
  57 |         from rag.authorization.evidence_filter import EvidenceFilter
  58 |         evidence_filter = EvidenceFilter()
  59 | 
  60 |         if scope:
  61 |             if not evidence_filter.is_authorized_for_policy(scope, policy):
  62 |                 return None
  63 | 
  64 |             t_date = getattr(scope, "target_date", None)
  65 |             s_date = getattr(scope, "start_date", None)
  66 |             e_date = getattr(scope, "end_date", None)
  67 |             req_ver = getattr(scope, "requested_version", None)
  68 | 
  69 |             if req_ver:
  70 |                 if str(version.version_num) != str(req_ver) and version.version_label != req_ver and f"v{version.version_num}" != req_ver:
  71 |                     return None
  72 |             elif s_date or e_date:
  73 |                 if not version.is_valid_for_interval(s_date, e_date):
  74 |                     return None
  75 |             elif t_date:
  76 |                 if not version.is_valid_for_date(t_date):
  77 |                     return None
  78 |             elif getattr(scope, "current_only", True) and not getattr(scope, "historical", False):
  79 |                 if not version.is_active and str(policy.status).lower() not in ("active", "published"):
  80 |                     return None
  81 | 
  82 |         section = chunk.section_path or "General"
  83 |         page = chunk.page or 1
  84 | 
  85 |         citations = [{
  86 |             "policy_id": policy.id,
  87 |             "version_id": version.id,
  88 |             "policy_name": policy.title,
  89 |             "version": version.version_number,
  90 |             "section": section,
  91 |             "page": page,
  92 |             "chunk_id": chunk.chunk_id
  93 |         }]
  94 | 
  95 |         return {
  96 |             "answer": ans.answer,
  97 |             "score": float(score),
  98 |             "confidence": float(ans.confidence if ans.confidence is not None else score),
  99 |             "matched_question": q_obj.question,
 100 |             "citations": citations,
 101 |             "policy": policy,
 102 |             "version": version,
 103 |             "source_chunk_ids": ans.source_chunk_ids,
 104 |             "source_chunk": chunk
 105 |         }

   1 | """
   2 | rag/retrieval/reranker.py
   3 | CrossEncoder reranker with device control and CPU fallback.
   4 | """
   5 | import os
   6 | import logging
   7 | from typing import List, Dict, Any
   8 | 
   9 | logger = logging.getLogger("rag.retrieval.reranker")
  10 | 
  11 | def _get_target_device(env_var: str = "RERANKER_DEVICE") -> str:
  12 |     device = os.environ.get(env_var)
  13 |     if device:
  14 |         return device
  15 |     import sys
  16 |     if sys.version_info >= (3, 14):
  17 |         return "cpu"
  18 |     import torch
  19 |     if torch.cuda.is_available():
  20 |         try:
  21 |             torch.zeros(1).cuda()
  22 |             return "cuda"
  23 |         except Exception:
  24 |             return "cpu"
  25 |     return "cpu"
  26 | 
  27 | class Qwen3Reranker:
  28 |     MODEL_NAME = "Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B"
  29 |     
  30 |     def __init__(self):
  31 |         self.device = _get_target_device("RERANKER_DEVICE")
  32 |         try:
  33 |             from sentence_transformers import CrossEncoder
  34 |             self._model = CrossEncoder(self.MODEL_NAME, device=self.device)
  35 |             logger.info(f"Loaded CrossEncoder {self.MODEL_NAME} on {self.device}")
  36 |         except Exception as e:
  37 |             logger.warning(f"Failed to load CrossEncoder {self.MODEL_NAME} on {self.device}: {e}. Retrying on CPU.")
  38 |             try:
  39 |                 from sentence_transformers import CrossEncoder
  40 |                 self._model = CrossEncoder(self.MODEL_NAME, device="cpu")
  41 |                 self.device = "cpu"
  42 |             except Exception as e2:
  43 |                 logger.error(f"Failed to load CrossEncoder on CPU: {e2}. Pass-through enabled.")
  44 |                 self._model = None
  45 | 
  46 |     def rank(self, query: str, candidates: List[Dict[str, Any]], top_k: int = 8) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
  47 |         if not candidates:
  48 |             return []
  49 | 
  50 |         if not self._model:

# [130/275] FILE: rag/retrieval/hybrid.py
# Language: Python | Lines: 1 to 56 | SHA-256: a058c5b2760e2aed4ec707fc09d2e68149281abab3d19ddca2328766823b05f3
################################################################################

   1 | """
   2 | rag/retrieval/hybrid.py
   3 | Hybrid Dense + BM25 retrieval with calibrated Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF).
   4 | """
   5 | from typing import List, Dict, Any
   6 | from rag.retrieval.dense import DenseRetriever
   7 | from rag.retrieval.sparse import PersistentBM25Index
   8 | 
   9 | class HybridRetriever:
  10 |     def __init__(self):
  11 |         self.dense = DenseRetriever()
  12 |         self.sparse = PersistentBM25Index()
  13 | 
  14 |     def search(self, query: str, filters: dict = None, top_k: int = 50) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
  15 |         dense_results = self.dense.search(query, filters, top_k=top_k)
  16 |         sparse_results = self.sparse.get_scores(query, filters)
  17 |         
  18 |         # RRF Fusion
  19 |         K = 60
  20 |         combined = {}
  21 |         
  22 |         for i, doc in enumerate(dense_results):
  23 |             doc_id = doc.get("chunk_id") or doc.get("id")
  24 |             combined[doc_id] = {
  25 |                 "doc": doc,
  26 |                 "score": 1.0 / (K + i + 1),
  27 |                 "dense_rank": i + 1,
  28 |                 "sparse_rank": None
  29 |             }
  30 |             
  31 |         for i, (doc_id, score, doc) in enumerate(sparse_results[:top_k]):
  32 |             if doc_id in combined:
  33 |                 combined[doc_id]["score"] += 1.0 / (K + i + 1)
  34 |                 combined[doc_id]["sparse_rank"] = i + 1
  35 |             else:
  36 |                 combined[doc_id] = {
  37 |                     "doc": doc,
  38 |                     "score": 1.0 / (K + i + 1),
  39 |                     "dense_rank": None,
  40 |                     "sparse_rank": i + 1
  41 |                 }
  42 |                 
  43 |         # Sort by RRF score
  44 |         fused = sorted(combined.values(), key=lambda x: x["score"], reverse=True)
  45 |         
  46 |         # Normalize fusion score to 0..1 range (max theoretical RRF score = 2 / (K + 1) ≈ 0.0328)
  47 |         max_possible_rrf = 2.0 / (K + 1)
  48 |         final_results = []
  49 |         for item in fused[:top_k]:
  50 |             doc = dict(item["doc"])
  51 |             normalized_score = min(1.0, item["score"] / max_possible_rrf)
  52 |             doc["hybrid_score"] = float(normalized_score)
  53 |             doc["raw_rrf_score"] = float(item["score"])
  54 |             final_results.append(doc)
  55 |             
  56 |         return final_results

# [END OF FILE: rag/retrieval/hybrid.py | Disclosed Lines: 56/56]

  27 | class Qwen3Reranker:

  46 |     def rank(self, query: str, candidates: List[Dict[str, Any]], top_k: int = 8) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
  47 |         if not candidates:
  48 |             return []
  49 | 
  50 |         if not self._model:
  51 |             return candidates[:top_k]
  52 | 
  53 |         try:
  54 |             # Score top candidates to keep CPU latency low
  55 |             eval_candidates = candidates[:min(len(candidates), 16)]
  56 |             pairs = [(query, c.get("text", "")) for c in eval_candidates]
  57 |             scores = self._model.predict(pairs)
  58 |             
  59 |             ranked = sorted(zip(scores, eval_candidates), reverse=True, key=lambda x: x[0])
  60 |             
  61 |             results = []
  62 |             for s, c in ranked[:top_k]:
  63 |                 c_copy = dict(c)
  64 |                 c_copy["rerank_score"] = float(s)
  65 |                 results.append(c_copy)
  66 |             return results
  67 |         except Exception as e:

  69 |             return candidates[:top_k]

  72 |         return self.rank(query, candidates, top_k=top_k)
  73 | 
  74 | class FlashRankReranker:
  75 |     def __init__(self, model_name: str = "ms-marco-TinyBERT-L-2-v2"):
  76 |         self.model_name = model_name

  87 |         if not candidates:
  88 |             return []
  89 |         if not self._ranker:
  90 |             return candidates[:top_k]
  91 |         try:
  92 |             passages = [{"id": i, "text": c.get("text", "")} for i, c in enumerate(candidates)]

   1 | """
   2 | rag/retrieval/sparse.py
   3 | Persistent BM25 sparse keyword retriever with incremental delta updates, partition filtering, and revision tracking.
   4 | """
   5 | import pickle
   6 | import os
   7 | import re
   8 | import logging
   9 | from typing import List, Tuple, Dict, Any, Optional
  10 | from rank_bm25 import BM25Okapi
  11 | from models import PolicyChunkV2
  12 | 
  13 | logger = logging.getLogger("rag.retrieval.sparse")
  14 | 
  15 | class PersistentBM25Index:
  16 |     INDEX_PATH = "data/bm25_index.pkl"
  17 |     
  18 |     def __init__(self):
  19 |         self._bm25 = None
  20 |         self._corpus: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
  21 |         self._revision = 0
  22 |         self.load()
  23 | 
  24 |     def load(self):
  25 |         if os.path.exists(self.INDEX_PATH):
  26 |             try:
  27 |                 with open(self.INDEX_PATH, 'rb') as f:
  28 |                     data = pickle.load(f)
  29 |                     self._bm25 = data['bm25']
  30 |                     self._corpus = data['corpus']
  31 |                     self._revision = data.get('revision', 0)
  32 |                 logger.info(f"Loaded persistent BM25 index with {len(self._corpus)} documents (revision {self._revision})")
  33 |                 return
  34 |             except Exception as e:
  35 |                 logger.error(f"Failed to load BM25 index from {self.INDEX_PATH}: {e}. Rebuilding...")
  36 |         self.rebuild_from_db()
  37 | 
  38 |     def save(self):
  39 |         try:
  40 |             os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(self.INDEX_PATH), exist_ok=True)
  41 |             tmp_path = self.INDEX_PATH + ".tmp"
  42 |             with open(tmp_path, 'wb') as f:
  43 |                 pickle.dump({
  44 |                     'bm25': self._bm25,
  45 |                     'corpus': self._corpus,
  46 |                     'revision': self._revision
  47 |                 }, f)
  48 |             os.replace(tmp_path, self.INDEX_PATH)
  49 |         except Exception as e:
  50 |             logger.error(f"Failed to save BM25 index: {e}")
  51 | 
  52 |     def rebuild_from_db(self):
  53 |         try:
  54 |             chunks = PolicyChunkV2.query.all()
  55 |             if not chunks:
  56 |                 self._corpus = []
  57 |                 self._bm25 = None
  58 |                 return
  59 |                 
  60 |             corpus = []
  61 |             tokenized_corpus = []
  62 |             for chunk in chunks:
  63 |                 tokens = re.findall(r"\b\w+\b", chunk.text.lower())
  64 |                 tokenized_corpus.append(tokens)
  65 |                 corpus.append({
  66 |                     "id": chunk.chunk_id,
  67 |                     "chunk_id": chunk.chunk_id,
  68 |                     "text": chunk.text,
  69 |                     "policy_id": chunk.policy_id,
  70 |                     "version_id": chunk.version_id,
  71 |                     "version": str(chunk.version_id),
  72 |                     "section": chunk.section_path or "General",
  73 |                     "section_path": chunk.section_path or "General",
  74 |                     "page": chunk.page or 1
  75 |                 })
  76 |                 
  77 |             self._bm25 = BM25Okapi(tokenized_corpus)
  78 |             self._corpus = corpus
  79 |             self._revision += 1
  80 |             self.save()
  81 |             logger.info(f"Rebuilt BM25 index with {len(corpus)} chunks (revision {self._revision})")
  82 |         except Exception as e:
  83 |             logger.error(f"Failed to rebuild BM25 from DB: {e}")
  84 | 
  85 |     def update_policy_version(self, policy_id: int, version_id: int, new_chunks: List[Dict[str, Any]]):
  86 |         """
  87 |         Incremental delta update: replaces/inserts chunks for a single policy version
  88 |         without rebuilding the entire database.
  89 |         """
  90 |         # Remove existing chunks for this version
  91 |         filtered_corpus = [c for c in self._corpus if not (c.get("policy_id") == policy_id and c.get("version_id") == version_id)]
  92 |         
  93 |         # Add new chunks
  94 |         for chunk in new_chunks:
  95 |             filtered_corpus.append({
  96 |                 "id": chunk.get("chunk_id") or chunk.get("id"),
  97 |                 "chunk_id": chunk.get("chunk_id") or chunk.get("id"),
  98 |                 "text": chunk.get("text", ""),
  99 |                 "policy_id": policy_id,
 100 |                 "version_id": version_id,
 101 |                 "version": str(chunk.get("version", version_id)),
 102 |                 "section": chunk.get("section") or chunk.get("section_path") or "General",
 103 |                 "section_path": chunk.get("section_path") or chunk.get("section") or "General",
 104 |                 "page": chunk.get("page", 1)
 105 |             })
 106 | 
 107 |         self._corpus = filtered_corpus
 108 |         if self._corpus:
 109 |             tokenized = [re.findall(r"\b\w+\b", c["text"].lower()) for c in self._corpus]
 110 |             self._bm25 = BM25Okapi(tokenized)
 111 |         else:
 112 |             self._bm25 = None
 113 |         self._revision += 1
 114 |         self.save()
 115 |         logger.info(f"Incrementally updated BM25 for policy {policy_id} v{version_id} ({len(new_chunks)} chunks, rev {self._revision})")
 116 | 
 117 |     def delete_policy_version(self, policy_id: int, version_id: int):
 118 |         """Incremental deletion for a policy version."""
 119 |         self._corpus = [c for c in self._corpus if not (c.get("policy_id") == policy_id and c.get("version_id") == version_id)]
 120 |         if self._corpus:
 121 |             tokenized = [re.findall(r"\b\w+\b", c["text"].lower()) for c in self._corpus]
 122 |             self._bm25 = BM25Okapi(tokenized)
 123 |         else:
 124 |             self._bm25 = None
 125 |         self._revision += 1
 126 |         self.save()
 127 | 
 128 |     def get_scores(self, query: str, filters: dict = None, scope: Any = None) -> List[Tuple[str, float, dict]]:
 129 |         if not self._bm25 or not self._corpus:
 130 |             self.load()
 131 |         if not self._bm25 or not self._corpus:
 132 |             return []
 133 |             
 134 |         tokenized_query = re.findall(r"\b\w+\b", query.lower())
 135 |         if not tokenized_query:
 136 |             return []
 137 |         doc_scores = self._bm25.get_scores(tokenized_query)
 138 |         
 139 |         results = []
 140 |         for i, score in enumerate(doc_scores):
 141 |             if score > 0:
 142 |                 doc = self._corpus[i]
 143 |                 
 144 |                 # Scope-based pre-filtering
 145 |                 if scope:
 146 |                     if getattr(scope, "allowed_policy_ids", None) is not None:
 147 |                         if doc.get("policy_id") not in scope.allowed_policy_ids:
 148 |                             continue
 149 |                     if getattr(scope, "allowed_version_ids", None) is not None:
 150 |                         if doc.get("version_id") not in scope.allowed_version_ids:
 151 |                             continue
 152 | 
 153 |                 # Pre-filtered partition matching
 154 |                 if filters:
 155 |                     match = True
 156 |                     for k, v in filters.items():
 157 |                         if isinstance(v, list):
 158 |                             if str(doc.get(k)) not in [str(x) for x in v]:
 159 |                                 match = False
 160 |                                 break
 161 |                         elif str(doc.get(k)) != str(v):
 162 |                             match = False
 163 |                             break
 164 |                     if not match:
 165 |                         continue
 166 |                         
 167 |                 results.append((doc["id"], float(score), doc))
 168 |                 
 169 |         return sorted(results, key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
 170 |         
 171 |     @property
 172 |     def revision(self) -> int:
 173 |         return self._revision

  23 |

  28 |         elif intent == Intent.SEARCH:

   1 | """
   2 | rag/router/intent_classifier.py
   3 | Classifies user query intent across 7 distinct operational routes.
   4 | """
   5 | import re
   6 | from enum import Enum
   7 | from typing import Tuple, Dict, Any
   8 | 
   9 | class Intent(str, Enum):
  10 |     FACT = "FACT"
  11 |     COMPILED_QA = "COMPILED_QA"

  16 |     REASONING = "REASONING"
  17 |     UNKNOWN = "UNKNOWN"
  18 | 
  19 | class IntentClassifier:
  20 |     COMPARISON_PATTERNS = [
  21 |         r"\b(?:compare|difference|changed|changes|versus|vs|diff|updated from|between v\d+ and v\d+)\b",
  22 |         r"\bwhat changed\b",
  23 |         r"\bhow is .* different from\b"
  24 |     ]
  25 |     
  26 |     TEMPORAL_PATTERNS = [
  27 |         r"\b(?:in 20\d\d|as of|effective date|historical|previous version|prior policy|back in|when was .* enacted|old version)\b",
  28 |         r"\b(?:january|february|march|april|may|june|july|august|september|october|november|december)\s+20\d\d\b",
  29 |         r"\bv\d+\b"
  30 |     ]
  31 |     
  32 |     FACT_PATTERNS = [
  33 |         r"\b(?:how many|how much|what is the limit|maximum amount|per diem|number of days|working hours|notice period|probation period|gift limit)\b",
  34 |         r"\b(?:amount|percentage|threshold|allowance|entitlement)\b"
  35 |     ]
  36 |     
  37 |     REASONING_PATTERNS = [
  38 |         r"\b(?:what if|suppose|scenario|if i transfer|how does .* affect|consequences|exception to|is it allowed if)\b",
  39 |         r"\b(?:eligible if|can i also|hypothetical)\b"
  40 |     ]
  41 | 
  42 |     MULTI_POLICY_PATTERNS = [
  43 |         r"\b(?:both|and also|across policies|travel and expense.*leave|security.*conduct)\b"
  44 |     ]
  45 | 
  46 |     def classify(self, query: str) -> Tuple[Intent, float]:
  47 |         q = query.lower()
  48 |         
  49 |         # 1. Comparison
  50 |         for pattern in self.COMPARISON_PATTERNS:
  51 |             if re.search(pattern, q):
  52 |                 return Intent.COMPARISON, 0.95
  53 |                 
  54 |         # 2. Temporal
  55 |         for pattern in self.TEMPORAL_PATTERNS:
  56 |             if re.search(pattern, q):
  57 |                 return Intent.TEMPORAL, 0.90
  58 | 
  59 |         # 3. Reasoning / What-if
  60 |         for pattern in self.REASONING_PATTERNS:
  61 |             if re.search(pattern, q):
  62 |                 return Intent.REASONING, 0.85
  63 | 
  64 |         # 4. Multi-policy
  65 |         for pattern in self.MULTI_POLICY_PATTERNS:
  66 |             if re.search(pattern, q):
  67 |                 return Intent.MULTI_POLICY, 0.80
  68 | 
  69 |         # 5. Direct Fact
  70 |         for pattern in self.FACT_PATTERNS:
  71 |             if re.search(pattern, q):
  72 |                 return Intent.FACT, 0.90
  73 | 
  74 |         # 6. Default to Search / Semantic QA
  75 |         if len(q.split()) <= 6 and q.startswith(("what is", "how to", "who is", "where is", "can i")):
  76 |             return Intent.COMPILED_QA, 0.75
  77 |             
  78 |         return Intent.SEARCH, 0.70

# [END OF FILE: rag/router/intent_classifier.py | Disclosed Lines: 78/78]

   1 | """
   2 | rag/router/query_router.py

   4 | """

  11 | class QueryRouter:

  16 | 
  17 |     def normalize(self, query: str) -> str:
  18 |         """Normalizes whitespace, punctuation, and common variants."""
  19 |         q = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", query.strip())
  20 |         q = re.sub(r"[?!.,;]+$", "", q)
  21 |         return q
  22 | 
  23 |     def route(self, query: str) -> Tuple[Intent, ComplexityLevel, str, Dict[str, Any]]:

  33 |             "intent_confidence": intent_conf,
  34 |             "normalized_query": normalized,

# [136/275] FILE: rag/router/temporal_router.py
# Language: Python | Lines: 1 to 45 | SHA-256: 659e885e863ae4f2116c533412696d9c61b7ca63f1f44991eab2bb73bce430b4
################################################################################

   1 | """
   2 | rag/router/temporal_router.py
   3 | Routes temporal and version comparison queries by identifying target dates and version numbers.
   4 | """
   5 | import re
   6 | from datetime import datetime, date
   7 | from typing import Optional, Tuple, List, Dict, Any
   8 | from models import Policy, PolicyVersion
   9 | 
  10 | class TemporalRouter:
  11 |     VERSION_DIFF_PATTERN = re.compile(r"\bv(\d+)\s*(?:and|vs|versus|to|\-)\s*v(\d+)\b", re.I)
  12 |     SINGLE_VERSION_PATTERN = re.compile(r"\bv(\d+)\b", re.I)
  13 |     YEAR_PATTERN = re.compile(r"\b(19|20)\d{2}\b")
  14 | 
  15 |     def route_temporal_query(self, query: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
  16 |         result = {
  17 |             "is_comparison": False,
  18 |             "version_v1": None,
  19 |             "version_v2": None,
  20 |             "target_version": None,
  21 |             "target_year": None,
  22 |             "is_historic": False
  23 |         }
  24 | 
  25 |         # Check for version diff (e.g. "v1 vs v2", "between v3 and v4")
  26 |         diff_match = self.VERSION_DIFF_PATTERN.search(query)
  27 |         if diff_match:
  28 |             result["is_comparison"] = True
  29 |             result["version_v1"] = int(diff_match.group(1))
  30 |             result["version_v2"] = int(diff_match.group(2))
  31 |             return result
  32 | 
  33 |         # Check for single version reference (e.g. "in v2")
  34 |         v_match = self.SINGLE_VERSION_PATTERN.search(query)
  35 |         if v_match:
  36 |             result["target_version"] = int(v_match.group(1))
  37 |             result["is_historic"] = True
  38 | 
  39 |         # Check for year
  40 |         y_match = self.YEAR_PATTERN.search(query)
  41 |         if y_match:
  42 |             result["target_year"] = int(y_match.group(0))
  43 |             result["is_historic"] = True
  44 | 
  45 |         return result

# [END OF FILE: rag/router/temporal_router.py | Disclosed Lines: 45/45]

  74 |             except Exception:
  75 |                 pass
  76 |             self._col = self._client.create_collection(

  86 |     def upsert_chunks(self, chunks: List[dict], embeddings: List[List[float]]):
  87 |         if not chunks or not embeddings:
  88 |             return
  89 |         ids = [c["chunk_id"] if "chunk_id" in c else f"chunk_{c.get('policy_id')}_{c.get('version')}_{c.get('chunk_index')}" for c in chunks]

  91 |         documents = [c.get("text", "") for c in chunks]

  95 |             for k, v in c.items():
  96 |                 if k != "text" and v is not None:
  97 |                     m[k] = str(v) if not isinstance(v, (str, int, float, bool)) else v
  98 |             metadatas.append(m)

 102 |         except Exception as e:

 104 |             self._client.delete_collection(name=self.col_name)
 105 |             self._col = self._client.create_collection(name=self.col_name, metadata={"hnsw:space": "cosine"})
 106 |             self._col.upsert(ids=ids, documents=documents, embeddings=embeddings, metadatas=metadatas)
 107 | 
 108 |     def delete_policy_version(self, policy_id: int, version: str):
 109 |         try:
 110 |             results = self._col.get(where={"$and": [
 111 |                 {"policy_id": {"$eq": str(policy_id)}},
 112 |                 {"version": {"$eq": str(version)}},
 113 |             ]})
 114 |             if results and results["ids"]:
 115 |                 self._col.delete(ids=results["ids"])
 116 |         except Exception:
 117 |             pass
 118 | 
 119 |     def delete_policy(self, policy_id: int):
 120 |         try:
 121 |             results = self._col.get(where={"policy_id": {"$eq": str(policy_id)}})
 122 |             if results and results["ids"]:
 123 |                 self._col.delete(ids=results["ids"])
 124 |         except Exception:
 125 |             pass
 126 | 
 127 |     def search(self, embedding: List[float], filters: dict, top_k: int = 50) -> List[dict]:
 128 |         if embedding and len(embedding) != self.embedding_dimension:
 129 |             raise ValueError(
 130 |                 f"Embedding dimension mismatch: query vector has {len(embedding)} dimensions, "
 131 |                 f"but vector store '{self.col_name}' requires {self.embedding_dimension} dimensions ({self.embedding_model})."
 132 |             )
 133 |         where = self._build_where(filters)
 134 |         n_results = min(top_k, max(self._col.count(), 1))
 135 |         if n_results == 0:
 136 |             return []
 137 |             
 138 |         try:
 139 |             results = self._col.query(
 140 |                 query_embeddings=[embedding],
 141 |                 n_results=n_results,
 142 |                 where=where if where else None,
 143 |                 include=["documents", "metadatas", "distances"],
 144 |             )
 145 |         except Exception as e:
 146 |             logger.error(f"Chroma query failed: {e}")
 147 |             return []
 148 |             
 149 |         hits = []
 150 |         if results and results["ids"] and len(results["ids"]) > 0:
 151 |             for i, doc_id in enumerate(results["ids"][0]):
 152 |                 meta = dict(results["metadatas"][0][i])
 153 |                 meta["id"] = doc_id
 154 |                 meta["chunk_id"] = doc_id
 155 |                 meta["text"] = results["documents"][0][i]
 156 |                 meta["score"] = max(0.0, 1.0 - float(results["distances"][0][i]))
 157 |                 hits.append(meta)
 158 |         return hits
 159 | 
 160 |     def _build_where(self, filters: dict):
 161 |         if not filters:
 162 |             return None
 163 |         conditions = []
 164 |         for k, v in filters.items():
 165 |             if isinstance(v, list):
 166 |                 conditions.append({k: {"$in": [str(x) for x in v]}})
 167 |             else:
 168 |                 conditions.append({k: {"$eq": str(v)}})
 169 |         if not conditions:
 170 |             return None
 171 |         if len(conditions) == 1:
 172 |             return conditions[0]
 173 |         return {"$and": conditions}
 174 | 
 175 |     def count(self) -> int:
 176 |         return self._col.count()
 177 | 
 178 |     def stats(self) -> dict:
 179 |         return {
 180 |             "total_chunks": self._col.count(),
 181 |             "collection": self.col_name,
 182 |             "path": CHROMA_PATH,
 183 |             "model": "chromadb",
 184 |         }
 185 | 
 186 | _store = None
 187 | def get_store() -> VectorStoreBase:
 188 |     global _store
 189 |     if _store is None:
 190 |         _store = VectorStore()
 191 |     return _store

   9 | class CitationValidator:

  13 |     def validate_and_enrich(self, raw_citations: List[Dict[str, Any]], scope: Optional[Any] = None) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
  14 |         """
  15 |         Validate and enrich citation list with authoritative database records.
  16 |         Strict invariant: Every citation MUST resolve to an actual Policy and PolicyVersion,
  17 |         and must be authorized for the user scope when scope is provided.
  18 |         Invalid, fabricated, or inaccessible records are dropped.
  19 |         """
  20 |         if not raw_citations:
  21 |             return []
  22 | 
  23 |         from rag.authorization.evidence_filter import EvidenceFilter
  24 |         evidence_filter = EvidenceFilter()
  25 | 
  26 |         validated = []
  27 |         seen = set()
  28 | 
  29 |         for cit in raw_citations:
  30 |             policy_id = cit.get("policy_id")
  31 |             version_id = cit.get("version_id")

  40 |                 if chunk:

  42 |                     version = db.session.get(PolicyVersion, chunk.version_id)
  43 |                     section = chunk.section_path or cit.get("section") or "General"
  44 |                     page = chunk.page or cit.get("page") or 1
  45 |                 else:
  46 |                     section = cit.get("section") or "General"
  47 |                     page = cit.get("page") or 1
  48 |             else:
  49 |                 section = cit.get("section") or "General"
  50 |                 page = cit.get("page") or 1
  51 | 
  52 |             # 2. Resolve via policy_id if not found via chunk
  53 |             if not policy and policy_id:

  55 |                     policy = db.session.get(Policy, int(policy_id))
  56 |                 except (ValueError, TypeError):
  57 |                     pass
  58 |

  62 |

# [140/275] FILE: rag/verification/confidence.py
# Language: Python | Lines: 1 to 103 | SHA-256: 502ea4fd0bef67d556c7e5bda0317dda4f756df91be7b6eca19c430d148a9bc2
################################################################################

   1 | """
   2 | rag/verification/confidence.py
   3 | Calibrated multi-factor confidence scoring combining retrieval score, evidence coverage, version clarity, and entailment.
   4 | """
   5 | import re
   6 | from typing import List, Dict, Any, Optional
   7 | from dataclasses import dataclass
   8 | from rag.engine.evidence_pack import EvidencePack
   9 | 
  10 | @dataclass
  11 | class ConfidenceScore:
  12 |     value: float
  13 |     high: bool
  14 |     abstain: bool
  15 |     retrieval_score: float
  16 |     coverage_score: float
  17 | 
  18 | class ConfidenceEngine:
  19 |     HIGH_THRESHOLD = 0.65
  20 |     LOW_THRESHOLD = 0.25
  21 |     
  22 |     STOPWORDS = {"what", "when", "where", "which", "who", "whom", "how", "why", "does", "have", "policy", "the", "for", "and", "can", "are", "get", "with", "from", "that", "this", "our", "you", "your", "will", "shall"}
  23 | 
  24 |     def _stem(self, word: str) -> str:
  25 |         w = word.lower()
  26 |         for suffix in ("ing", "ed", "es", "s", "ly", "ment", "tion", "able", "ive"):
  27 |             if len(w) > len(suffix) + 3 and w.endswith(suffix):
  28 |                 return w[:-len(suffix)]
  29 |         return w
  30 | 
  31 |     def score(self, query: str, evidence: EvidencePack) -> ConfidenceScore:
  32 |         if not evidence.chunks or not evidence.scores:
  33 |             return ConfidenceScore(
  34 |                 value=0.0, high=False, abstain=True, retrieval_score=0.0, coverage_score=0.0
  35 |             )
  36 | 
  37 |         retrieval_conf = self._retrieval_confidence(evidence.scores)
  38 |         coverage_conf = self._evidence_coverage(query, evidence.chunks)
  39 |         
  40 |         # Weighted combination: 55% retrieval rank, 45% evidence coverage
  41 |         raw_final = (retrieval_conf * 0.55) + (coverage_conf * 0.45)
  42 |         
  43 |         # Apply Isotonic Calibration to fix overconfidence (Brier/ECE)
  44 |         final = self._isotonic_calibrate(raw_final)
  45 |         
  46 |         # Abstain if evidence coverage is low or composite confidence is below calibrated baseline
  47 |         abstain = (coverage_conf < 0.25) or (retrieval_conf < 0.20) or (final < self.LOW_THRESHOLD)
  48 |             
  49 |         return ConfidenceScore(
  50 |             value=float(min(1.0, max(0.0, final))),
  51 |             high=final >= self.HIGH_THRESHOLD,
  52 |             abstain=abstain,
  53 |             retrieval_score=retrieval_conf,
  54 |             coverage_score=coverage_conf
  55 |         )
  56 | 
  57 |     def _isotonic_calibrate(self, raw_score: float) -> float:
  58 |         """
  59 |         Applies a piecewise linear Isotonic Regression curve mapped from validation data.
  60 |         Brings Expected Calibration Error (ECE) down and improves Brier Score.
  61 |         """
  62 |         # Pre-fitted isotonic knots from validation (raw_score -> calibrated_prob)
  63 |         knots = [
  64 |             (0.00, 0.00),
  65 |             (0.30, 0.10),
  66 |             (0.50, 0.25),
  67 |             (0.70, 0.45),
  68 |             (0.85, 0.70),
  69 |             (0.95, 0.85),
  70 |             (1.00, 0.95)
  71 |         ]
  72 |         
  73 |         for i in range(len(knots) - 1):
  74 |             x1, y1 = knots[i]
  75 |             x2, y2 = knots[i+1]
  76 |             if x1 <= raw_score <= x2:
  77 |                 # Linear interpolation
  78 |                 return y1 + (y2 - y1) * ((raw_score - x1) / (x2 - x1))
  79 |         
  80 |         return max(0.0, min(1.0, raw_score))
  81 |         
  82 |     def _retrieval_confidence(self, scores: list) -> float:
  83 |         if not scores:
  84 |             return 0.0
  85 |         raw_max = max(scores)
  86 |         if raw_max < 0.05:
  87 |             return min(1.0, raw_max / 0.0328)
  88 |         return float(min(1.0, raw_max))
  89 |         
  90 |     def _evidence_coverage(self, query: str, chunks: list) -> float:
  91 |         if not chunks:
  92 |             return 0.0
  93 | 
  94 |         raw_words = [w for w in re.findall(r"\b[a-z0-9]+\b", query.lower()) if w not in self.STOPWORDS and len(w) > 1]
  95 |         if not raw_words:
  96 |             return 0.85
  97 | 
  98 |         stemmed_query = [self._stem(w) for w in raw_words]
  99 |         combined_text = " ".join([c.get("text", "").lower() for c in chunks])
 100 |         chunk_stems = set([self._stem(w) for w in re.findall(r"\b[a-z0-9]+\b", combined_text)])
 101 |         
 102 |         matched = sum(1 for s in stemmed_query if s in chunk_stems or any(s in cw for cw in chunk_stems))
 103 |         return matched / len(stemmed_query)

# [END OF FILE: rag/verification/confidence.py | Disclosed Lines: 103/103]

# [141/275] FILE: rag/verification/entailment.py

   1 | """
   2 | rag/verification/entailment.py
   3 | Entailment-based grounding check for RAG responses.
   4 | Provides EntailmentVerifier class with claim extraction and DeBERTa NLI scoring.
   5 | """
   6 | import re
   7 | import os
   8 | import logging
   9 | from typing import List, Dict, Any, Tuple
  10 | from dataclasses import dataclass
  11 | 
  12 | logger = logging.getLogger("rag.entailment")
  13 | 
  14 | @dataclass
  15 | class EntailmentResult:
  16 |     is_entailed: bool
  17 |     score: float
  18 |     verdict: str  # ENTAILMENT, CONTRADICTION, UNKNOWN
  19 |     failed_claims: List[str]
  20 | 
  21 | class EntailmentVerifier:
  22 |     def __init__(self):
  23 |         self.enabled = os.environ.get('ENTAILMENT_ENABLED', 'true').lower() == 'true'
  24 |         self._nli_model = None
  25 |         self._use_nli = True
  26 | 
  27 |     def _get_nli_model(self):
  28 |         if self._nli_model is None and self._use_nli:
  29 |             try:
  30 |                 from sentence_transformers import CrossEncoder
  31 |                 device = os.environ.get("RERANKER_DEVICE", "cpu")
  32 |                 self._nli_model = CrossEncoder("cross-encoder/nli-deberta-v3-base", device=device)
  33 |             except Exception as e:
  34 |                 logger.warning(f"Failed to load NLI model, falling back to lexical overlap: {e}")
  35 |                 self._use_nli = False
  36 |         return self._nli_model
  37 | 
  38 |     def split_into_claims(self, text: str) -> List[str]:
  39 |         # Strip markdown, citations, header boilerplate
  40 |         t = re.sub(r'\[Policy:[^\]]+\]', '', text)
  41 |         t = re.sub(r'^(?:[A-Z\s&—\-]+(?:POLICY|v\d+\.\d+))', '', t, flags=re.MULTILINE)
  42 |         t = re.sub(r'Effective Date:\s*[0-9\-]+', '', t)
  43 |         sentences = re.split(r'(?<=[.!?\n])\s+', t.strip())
  44 |         claims = []
  45 |         for s in sentences:
  46 |             s_clean = s.strip().lstrip("0123456789.- ")
  47 |             # Only evaluate substantive claims with verbs / facts
  48 |             if len(s_clean) >= 15 and not s_clean.startswith(("According to", "Based on", "Table of")):
  49 |                 claims.append(s_clean)
  50 |         return claims
  51 | 
  52 |     def verify(self, answer: str, chunks: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> EntailmentResult:
  53 |         if not self.enabled:
  54 |             return EntailmentResult(is_entailed=True, score=1.0, verdict="ENTAILMENT", failed_claims=[])
  55 |         if not answer or not chunks:
  56 |             return EntailmentResult(is_entailed=False, score=0.0, verdict="CONTRADICTION", failed_claims=["No evidence provided"])
  57 | 
  58 |         claims = self.split_into_claims(answer)
  59 |         if not claims:
  60 |             return EntailmentResult(is_entailed=True, score=1.0, verdict="ENTAILMENT", failed_claims=[])
  61 | 
  62 |         context = " ".join([c.get("text", "") for c in chunks])
  63 |         nli = self._get_nli_model()
  64 | 
  65 |         if nli:
  66 |             pairs = [(context, claim) for claim in claims]
  67 |             try:
  68 |                 scores = nli.predict(pairs)
  69 |                 import numpy as np
  70 |                 def softmax(x):
  71 |                     e_x = np.exp(x - np.max(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True))
  72 |                     return e_x / e_x.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True)
  73 | 
  74 |                 probs = softmax(scores) if len(scores.shape) > 1 else softmax(np.array([scores]))[0]
  75 |                 label2id = {k.lower(): v for k, v in nli.config.label2id.items()}
  76 |                 entailment_idx = label2id.get('entailment', 1)
  77 |                 contradiction_idx = label2id.get('contradiction', 0)
  78 | 
  79 |                 if len(probs.shape) > 1:
  80 |                     entailment_scores = probs[:, entailment_idx]
  81 |                     contra_scores = probs[:, contradiction_idx]
  82 |                 else:
  83 |                     entailment_scores = np.array([probs[entailment_idx]])
  84 |                     contra_scores = np.array([probs[contradiction_idx]])
  85 | 
  86 |                 avg_entail = float(entailment_scores.mean())
  87 |                 avg_contra = float(contra_scores.mean())
  88 | 
  89 |                 if avg_contra > 0.5:
  90 |                     verdict = "CONTRADICTION"
  91 |                     is_entailed = False
  92 |                 elif avg_entail > 0.35:
  93 |                     verdict = "ENTAILMENT"
  94 |                     is_entailed = True
  95 |                 else:
  96 |                     verdict = "UNKNOWN"
  97 |                     is_entailed = False
  98 | 
  99 |                 failed = [claims[i] for i, s in enumerate(entailment_scores) if s <= 0.35]
 100 |                 return EntailmentResult(is_entailed=is_entailed, score=avg_entail, verdict=verdict, failed_claims=failed)
 101 |             except Exception as e:
 102 |                 logger.error(f"Error in NLI predict: {e}")
 103 | 
 104 |         # Fallback when neural NLI model is unavailable
 105 |         # Lexical overlap measures token recall but cannot prove factual entailment.
 106 |         context_tokens = set(re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", context.lower()))
 107 |         claim_scores = []
 108 |         failed = []
 109 | 
 110 |         for claim in claims:
 111 |             claim_tokens = set(re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", claim.lower()))
 112 |             if not claim_tokens:
 113 |                 continue
 114 |             overlap = len(claim_tokens & context_tokens) / len(claim_tokens)
 115 |             claim_scores.append(overlap)
 116 |             if overlap < 0.25:
 117 |                 failed.append(claim)
 118 | 
 119 |         avg_overlap = sum(claim_scores) / max(len(claim_scores), 1)
 120 |         # Never manufacture factual entailment without neural NLI verification
 121 |         is_entailed = False
 122 |         verdict = "UNKNOWN"
 123 | 
 124 |         return EntailmentResult(is_entailed=is_entailed, score=avg_overlap, verdict=verdict, failed_claims=failed)
 125 | 
 126 | def verify_entailment(answer: str, chunks: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Tuple[bool, float]:
 127 |     verifier = EntailmentVerifier()
 128 |     res = verifier.verify(answer, chunks)
 129 |     return res.is_entailed, res.score

# [END OF FILE: rag/verification/entailment.py | Disclosed Lines: 129/129]
